correctness.rationale: Every paired-dominating size-2t set has the endpoint set of an indexed t-matching, and every dominating endpoint set of a t-matching qualifies. Exhaustive enumeration for t=1,2,3,4 gives counts 0,0,0,684. A separately structured full vertex-mask enumeration with a recursive perfect-matching test reproduces these numbers and independently reconstructs all transition graphs. Both programs assert and reproduce jump 3504 edges, connected component 684 with eccentricities 6:216,7:432,8:36; no token slides; loose pair substitution 2016 edges, component 630 plus 54 isolates, large component eccentricity 6; strict partner-preserving substitution 1392 edges, components 432,168,30 plus 54 isolates and per-component eccentricity profiles 432:(9:192,10:240),168:(9:96,10:72),30:(4:30). Every optimum meets each bipartition in four vertices, proving the absence of token slides. The isolate equivalence is directly checked against all induced-edge counts; exactly 54 have four induced edges and hence induce 4K2. Complete finite certificate and two standalone verifiers reproduce the critical computations. Finite conclusions only; no infinite inference.

value.rationale: A minimum paired-dominating set models a guard deployment with a matching of back-up partners. Its minimum cardinality does not decide whether different optimal deployments can be reached by individual relocations, adjacent sliding, or moving an entire pair while retaining other partnerships. On this classical cubic symmetric benchmark, the four rules exhibit genuinely different accessibility geometries: complete TJ reachability, total TS freezing, one large pair-substitution component plus 54 isolates, and three distinct components under partnership preservation. The exact induced-4K2 characterization explains which optima are frozen under pair moves. These exact natural invariants and structural boundary are motivated independent of their computation, without claiming an infinite-family theorem.
